utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-01-48-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Will both parties make their appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, counsel. For the Prosecution appear Mrs. Marie Tuma, trial attorney, Mr. Hasan Younis, trial support, and myself, Mr. Ekkehard Withopf, acting trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Withopf. You're not getting any interpretation. If the usher can check the circumstances. Now you are able to hear us? Could you make your appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not get the interpretation. Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could introduce yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I can hear now. Thank you. I am lead counsel for Mr. Sefer Halilovic in his Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I notice Ms. Kreho is appearing also as an assistant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KREHO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. This is the fifth Status Conference held in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And hopefully, the last one before we have the Pre-Trial Conference which is to be held in accordance with Rule 73 bis. Subsequent to the last Status Conference, which was held on 10th of February, Mr. Ahmed Hodzic was assigned as the Defence counsel replacing the previous Defence counsel for the accused pursuant to decision filed by the Registrar on 20th February this year. Both the pre-trial briefs of the Prosecution and the Defence have been filed. In addition, the Prosecution has filed its military expert report, and the translation of the postmortem examination reports and updated exhibit list. And thus, this case seems to be coming close to be ready for trial. Before we move on to more rudimentary matters of a Status Conference, I would like to turn directly to the issue of taking of a deposition pursuant to Rule 71. The Prosecution filed its motion to take the deposition of a terminally ill witness for use at trial on the 4th of March this year. Specifically, the Prosecution requested that the deposition be taken without the presence of the accused. Now, as far as the Chamber is aware, the issue of deliberately excluding the presence of the accused from the deposition process has not been raised in this international tribunal. This has been the case as the accused had been detained at the Detention Unit in other proceedings. Thus, the Trial Chamber found it prudent to look more closely at the motion, and accordingly, I issued a scheduling order allowing the Defence to file a response, and inviting the Registry to file its observations. The Defence filed a response on 8th of May this year basically agreeing with the Prosecution on all points except on the point of excluding the presence of the accused. The Registry filed its observations on the practical arrangement on 16th of May. Assessing from the memorandum the Registry presents two options, one being to have practically the entire Tribunal flown to Sarajevo; the other, to have only two, i.e., a technician and a court officer flown to Sarajevo. But then have the Defence counsel and accused flown to The Hague. However, speaking off the top of my head, I'm of the opinion that an arrangement somewhere in the middle can be made allowing the Defence counsel and the accused to remain in Sarajevo if we are to allow the accused to be present at all at the deposition. In the meanwhile, as the rule is written out in Rule 71, the issue of taking deposition is a matter for the Trial Chamber. Thus, I would like to make it clear that I will confer with the Chamber on the issues raised today before a decision is issued. Having said that, I would like first to hear from the Prosecution regarding these matters, specifically as to the reason why the accused should not be present at the deposition and as to the practical arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to going into details on this issue, the Prosecution is requesting closed session because we have to discuss a number of issues that relate to the health condition of the ill witness that may be crucial for the decision of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Private session, please. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To get to some practical information, how long do you expect your examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a very difficult question to answer. The interview in December, as you know, took three days caused by the numerous breaks that had been necessary. We anticipate a very similar situation this time as well, so we anticipate the examination-in-chief lasting for at least two to two and a half days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I shall confer with the Trial Chamber once again about this matter, and the Chamber will give its ruling after having the Senior Legal Officer prepare some practical arrangement in cooperation with the Registry and the Prosecution. Speaking for myself, the sooner the deposition would take place, the better it would be. The target date I have in mind, sometime in late June. Let's get moving to the pre-trial preparations. As for the Defence pre-trial brief, I appreciate the Defence counsel's effort to keep the same paragraph numbers as the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, thus making it easier for the reader to understand the difference of each party's position. However, I have to express my concerns regarding some Defence's filing. The Defence missed the deadline for filing response to the Prosecution's motion for taking of the deposition and was only able to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. file the response when I issued an order granting an extension of time. In addition, as the Prosecution pointed out in its filing of 22nd of April, the Defence has not followed the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions in filing its pre-trial brief. I will only stress this once, but it is an obligation of both parties, including the Defence, to be fully aware of all our rules in the Tribunal. So for the future, I expect the rules, including the practice direction, to be read carefully and to follow the directions accordingly. Mr. Hodzic, do you have anything to say about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I support what you have said. I wish, however, to draw your attention to the fact that just before filing this submission, I was appointed Defence counsel so that there was a certain lack of experience on my part. In future, our submissions will be in accordance with the rules and the prescribed procedure. This is as regards this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand. Now, I'd like to turn to the issue of disclosure. If Mr. Withopf could update myself, me and the Chamber generally as to the disclosure matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, since the last Status Conference, there have been a number of additional disclosures both under Rule 66(A)(2) and under Rule 68, on 3rd April and on 17th April, a number of witness statements and a number of documents have been disclosed to the Defence. What's even more important in respect to reciprocal disclosure, huge amounts of materials have been made available to the Defence for inspection at several locations, and another such reciprocal disclosure will take place tomorrow. In that respect, the Prosecution wishes to remind the Defence that reciprocal disclosure is actually a reciprocal disclosure as it says. The Defence to date has not complied with its obligations under Rule 67(C) to provide inspection of material to the Prosecution, although the Prosecution at several occasions locations has done all efforts to provide the Defence with access to the Prosecution's materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So is it your intention to take a look into the -- what is possessed by the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. I may draw your attention to the following fact: The Defence has attached to its pre-trial brief a list of exhibits, a list of witness statements. Under usual circumstances according to the rules, the Defence is not obliged to make such exhibits available to the Prosecution at this point in time. However, if Defence considers such materials to be in support of the Defence case, such material is material to the Defence case and falls as such under the obligation under Rule 67(C).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hodzic, are you in the position to answer this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel that cooperation between the Prosecution and Defence has so far consisted in our being disclosed materials in favour of my client. Something was promised at the last Status Conference that we have not received yet, and this is the expert report of the military expert for the Prosecution. Another problem we have is that we have a number of statements that have been disclosed to us, but not in a language that the accused understands. They are in the English language and have not been translated into Bosnian. All the material that we have is material that we have not evaluated as being material that we are obliged to disclose. And we have not received such requests. We are grateful to the Prosecution for allowing us to inspect a great amount of material which contains evidence that we would like to use, but we would like to draw attention to some issues that arise out of that at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order to update you, I'd like to tell you something. One of the former counsel, Mr. Balijagic, formally triggered the reciprocal disclosure obligation of Rule 67 by, if I'm correct, by notice filed on 1st of May in 2002. And this was adopted by Mr. Caglar at the Status Conference in October 2002, last year. And the Prosecution had also asked the Defence to provide criteria for searching the material so as to focus the searches more accurately. And arrangements were made for Mr. Caglar to inspect the so-called Seve files and the state surveillance files at the Prosecutor's Office in December 2002. If circumstances are such, then the Defence has a responsibility according to the rule of so-called reciprocal disclosure to provide the opportunity to the Prosecution to take a look into Defence documents. So putting aside the -- apart the disclosure of translation of witness statements, what would you say to this matter of reciprocal disclosure? I remember that Mr. Balijagic and Caglar, a number of cases, has said that there are some material documents which will prove that Mr. Halilovic would be innocent. So are you ready to show those documents to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I'm ready to do this and to disclose those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I'd like to the Prosecution to have contact with the Defence team to set a date and prepare for these practical arrangements. Shall I set a deadline for that, or it would be all right to leave the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution appreciates that the cooperation between the parties has significantly improved over the last few months, especially since Mr. Hodzic has been assigned, so the Prosecution thinks that it should be possible that the parties make the arrangements themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me briefly mention about the agreed facts. I noticed on the pre-trial brief from the Defence, even though it did not specifically mention what the agreed facts or the facts not in dispute are, but Defence deliberately omit some number of paragraphs which seems to be not in dispute. So I wonder whether the parties can develop a little bit further to produce in an orderly form of agreed or "not in dispute" facts. Do you think it's possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution thinks it's possible. There are several manners to do this. As you may recall, previous Defence counsel Mr. Balijagic has actually provided the Prosecution with a list of facts he would agree. It is not clear to the Prosecution to date as to whether the current Defence will actually agree to these facts as well. The Prosecution suggests that Defence and Prosecution will meet on this issue and go through the number of facts that could be agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would very much encourage it. If there's anything you can add, Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to everything done by Mr. Balijagic, all the action taken by Mr. Balijagic, we are no longer prepared to accept these acts as legally valid, and I'll tell you why. We submitted to the Trial Chamber, you haven't received it yet, a request which concerned two issues. First of all, the application of Rule 65(K), and secondly concerning the conflict of interest between Mr. Balijagic. If possible, could we go into private session because this concerns some very serious issues, and we have to adopt a position with regard to these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was just informed that the motion by the Defence was missing some formalities and was returned and was filed very recently, just today. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the motion was not filed because it was missing pages. And if the counsel can please submit a new version to me, and I'll file it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me turn to the witness list briefly. The Prosecution has listed originally 94 witnesses, 52 live and 43 Rule 92 bis. And thereafter, the Prosecution filed two motions, one in 5th of February this year, and the last one being on 23rd of April this year. Together adding a total of five witnesses to the list, three live and two Rule 92 bis. And the statements of the four additional witnesses were disclosed to the Defence in October last year and should be in the possession of the current Defence counsel, and the statement of the last additional witness was disclosed to the Defence in April of this year. The Defence has not filed a response to either application. So may I take it that the Defence has no position to that motion?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat that sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could repeat your answer, please. The interpreter didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We accept the Prosecution's application, the suggestion with regard to the disclosure -- with regard to the suggested witnesses. We have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since there's no objection, the motions are granted. In one stage of this Status Conference, I remember that Prosecution has mentioned that it may file an addendum or change the pre-trial brief after you have got the new military expert opinion. What's the status now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, your recollection is correct. The Prosecution, however, based on the military expert report doesn't see the need to file an addendum to the pre-trial brief. However, as I mentioned, we will get an additional expert report within the next few weeks. If the need would arise, the Prosecution would file an addendum to its pre-trial brief. If I may use the opportunity in respect to Rule 92 bis witnesses, the Prosecution will add probably four to five additional witnesses to its witness list, and the respective Rule 92 bis declarations will be obtained probably in mid-June this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since you raised the Rule 92 bis witnesses, I wonder if the Defence has formed a kind of intention whether to agree or object to the admission of the 92 bis, whether with or without cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The situation is not quite clear to me with regard to the additional expert report and with regard to whether the suggested witnesses are going to be heard in relation to this report, or whether it's a matter of entirely new facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm dealing with now the -- the so-called 92 bis witness statements, in which case the witnesses are not usually supposed to come to the Court. Instead, their testimony will be given in written form under Rule 92 bis. So in that case, the actual determination will be better to be deferred to the actual Trial Chamber who will hear the case, but it's better for the Defence to be ready for their answer whether to agree or not. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree because I would like these witnesses to be examined live so that we could exercise our right to cross-examine the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will confer this matter with the Trial Chamber, whether to give a ruling now or defer -- actually, the Prosecution hasn't filed its motion officially. So I will confer this matter with the Chamber. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting. Your Honour, as a suggestion from the side of the Prosecution, we suggest to raise this issue of the admissibility of Rule 92 bis statements with Defence counsel at some near future. And the Prosecution is still optimistic, that at least with regard to a number of 92 bis statements there could be an agreement between the Defence and the Prosecution. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think I exhausted all the issues, but if there's any issues for the parties to raise, I'd like to hear it. From the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think you exhausted all pending issues from the Prosecution side. There's nothing else to discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hodzic, is there anything you'd like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to point out, to raise the issue yet again, the issue that concerns Mr. Balijagic because this could affect many other matters that have been dealt with, and I think a decision should be taken with regard to this matter. Apart from that, I have no other suggestions to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will read the motion later. I hope that everything is written in the motion. And I'll pass it on to the Trial Chamber. If you have anything to add to what is written in the motion, you can do so right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the moment, I have nothing to add since we have included all information we had in the submission. But I would like to point out immediately that we are still in the process of examining these documents. I don't know whether there will be any other documents that will support our claim, so at the moment, this is something we cannot express a position on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: May I see the Legal Officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One thing I'd like to raise is just before I entered this courtroom today, I was passed by the Senior Legal Officer a letter from the accused directed to the Presiding Judge of this Trial Chamber. When counsel is appointed, it is usual for a counsel to communicate with the Chamber, and I don't think it's an appropriate attitude for an accused to communicate directly with the Judges. So I'd like to ask the Defence counsel to let the accused bear in mind such attitude is not appropriate. And to wrap up today's Status Conference, the deposition will take place sometime in late June. And I'll recommend the Trial Chamber to have the Pre-Trial Conference to make the case be ready for trial in early July. And that -- unless there's anything the parties would like to raise, then the Status Conference is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: [Trial Chamber and Senior Legal Officer confer]
